prompt: An enterprise SaaS software vendor doubled the annual subscription price for its flagship CRM platform. prompt: A luxury wristwatch manufacturer slashed production output by fifty percent while raising the retail sticker price of its timepieces from $10,000 to $30,000, creating long retail waiting lists. prompt: A budget regional airline eliminated complimentary checked baggage and instituted a forty-dollar fee per bag. Within three months, total passenger bookings fell by five percent. prompt: A streaming media conglomerate raised its monthly subscription fee by 10% and spent ten million dollars acquiring exclusive rights to an acclaimed television drama series. Over the quarter, subscriber numbers grew by 2%. The head of finance declared that the content acquisition was directly responsible for the revenue growth. What alternative explanation undermines this claim?
answer: The ten percent price increase on loyal existing subscribers accounts for most of the revenue growth, while the new drama series attracted negligible net additions.
options: The ten percent price increase on loyal existing subscribers accounts for most of the revenue growth, while the new drama series attracted negligible net additions.
The television series received three nominations at an international entertainment awards ceremony.
The streaming service redesigned its mobile user interface to support portrait video playback.
Competitor streaming platforms also introduced original science-fiction documentary programming.
why: 營收拆解（量 × 價）：漲價 10%、訂戶 +2%，營收約成長 12%，其中約 10 個百分點來自既有訂戶付更多錢，新影集帶來的淨新增訂戶很少，因此不能把營收成長歸功於買下新影集。

prompt: A fast-food franchise chain introduced a 'One-Dollar Value Menu' to undercut competitors, resulting in a fifty percent spike in total customer foot traffic and record total gross revenue. options: The franchise launched a national television advertising campaign featuring animated mascots.

The franchise sourced paper beverage cups from a certified sustainable forestry supplier.
why: 自相殘殺效應 (Cannibalization)：低價產品侵蝕高利潤主產品線。

prompt: A pharmaceutical company held an exclusive patent on a life-saving respiratory inhaler, pricing it at $400 per unit while the unit manufacturing cost was $10. Faced with public outrage, the firm lowered the price to $100. Despite selling twice as many inhalers, gross profit from the inhaler fell by more than half. Why did gross profit decline?
answer: Because the price cut shrank the profit on each unit from $390 to $90, so unit sales would have needed to rise more than fourfold just to match the previous gross profit.
options: Because generic inhaler alternatives entered the market upon chemical patent expiry.
Because the corporate public relations department spent five million dollars on goodwill advertisements.
Because the price cut shrank the profit on each unit from $390 to $90, so unit sales would have needed to rise more than fourfold just to match the previous gross profit.
Because medical clinics stocked thirty days of inventory in warehouse distribution freezers.
why: 單位毛利由 $400−$10＝$390 降到 $100−$10＝$90。銷量只翻倍：2 × 90＝180，只有原本 390 的約 46%，毛利下降約 54%。要維持原本的毛利總額，銷量必須增加到約 4.3 倍（390 ÷ 90），翻倍遠遠不夠。

prompt: A subscription meal-kit startup doubled its customer acquisition marketing spend, driving a sixty percent increase in active registered paying households. However, customer lifetime value (LTV) dropped below customer acquisition cost (CAC). Why is this business trajectory unsustainable?

why: LTV（顧客終身價值）低於 CAC（取得一位顧客的成本），代表每多爭取一位顧客就虧一次錢；行銷預算加倍只會讓虧損與現金消耗擴大，因此無法持續。（業界常以 LTV 約為 CAC 的 3 倍作為健康參考，但那只是經驗法則。）
